audit_findings.title: Projected growth may omit the reinvestment required to produce it
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 expansionary and efficiency capex was $163 million, equal to 56.6% of $287.9 million anchor OE; growth adds $620 million to base and $1.348 billion to bull operating PV versus bear; required forecast reinvestment is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth increases forecast OE and terminal value; if the capital required to earn that growth is not deducted, operating PV is overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: We invested $269 million in capital expenditures, which was comprised of expansionary and efficiency capital expenditures, to support and grow our existing businesses, totaling $163 million, maintenance capital expenditures totaling $106 million, and $18 million invested in business combinations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that growth and efficiency projects consume substantial capital, but the supplied record does not demonstrate whether the DCF charges reinvestment. Because nearly half the base and bull values come from terminal value and the growth assumptions add $620 million to $1.348 billion of operating PV, the unresolved formula issue is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace every projected-year formula and rerun base and bull with explicit reinvestment tied to 15.5% RONTA, including terminal-period reinvestment; reconcile the charge to maintenance, expansionary, efficiency and acquisition spending without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may classify operating liquidity as surplus cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $643.593 million added to equity value, equal to $11.19 per share and 13.7% of base equity value; the non-surplus portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash or short-term investments required for working capital, committed projects, insurance capital or minimum liquidity should not be added as distributable surplus in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Consequently, our working capital increases during our first and second quarters resulting in negative or modest cash flows from operations during those periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge amount is verified as the latest $597.263 million of cash plus $46.330 million of investments, and it excludes separately reported restricted balances. However, the filing also reports a $169 million seasonal working-capital build and $108 million of capital-project commitments. Those facts do not prove that the bridge is wrong, but an unresolved classification affecting up to 13.7% of base equity value is reasonably capable of changing the valuation range.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $643.593 million line by line to unrestricted balances and establish a documented minimum operating-cash reserve after seasonal working capital, the $108 million project commitments, acquisition funding and captive-insurance requirements; rerun the bridge using only demonstrated surplus.

audit_findings.title: Deferred-compensation claims require a cash-versus-share settlement reconciliation
audit_findings.magnitude: $70.8 million total reported obligation, equal to $1.23 per valuation share and 1.5% of base equity value if entirely incremental
audit_findings.mechanism: A cash-settled portion would reduce the equity bridge; stock-settled obligations must be captured through legally outstanding shares rather than deducted again as cash claims.
audit_findings.evidence: Related liabilities totaled $ 70.8 million and $ 67.0 million on December 27, 2025 and December 28, 2024, respectively, and are included in Other liabilities and Shareholders’ equity.
audit_findings.explanation: Settlement classification remains unresolved, but the filing states that stock elections are funded with shares issued to a Rabbi trust, making those shares already legally outstanding, while the entire reported obligation is only $70.8 million. Even treating all of it as an additional cash claim would reduce base value by about $1.23 per share and the base-derived buy-below level by about $0.86, insufficient by itself to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the plan-level cash-versus-stock liability schedule, identify Rabbi-trust shares already included in outstanding shares, and confirm the 57.516116 million diluted-share ceiling includes all remaining stock-settled units without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Dempsey's exercisable put creates a contingent claim outside ordinary debt
audit_findings.magnitude: $50 million gross put price, equal to $0.87 per valuation share and 1.1% of base equity value; the latest carrying value of UFPI's existing 50% interest is $51.3 million; net economic burden is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Exercise would require a $50 million payment but would deliver the other 50% interest and its earnings; only the payment less the acquired interest's value belongs in the bridge, with OE adjusted consistently.
audit_findings.evidence: Per the contracts, the Sellers have a put right to sell their equity interest to us for $ 50 million and we have a call right to purchase the Seller’s equity interest for $ 70 million, which were both first exercisable in June 2025 and expire in June 2030.
audit_findings.explanation: Recognition and fair value remain unresolved, but even the gross compulsory payment before crediting the acquired interest is only 1.1% of base equity value. The net adjustment should be smaller if the acquired interest has positive value, so this item is not large enough by itself to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the put is recognized anywhere on the latest balance sheet, obtain Dempsey's current financials and fair value the sellers' 50% interest; adjust the bridge only for the net burden and include the corresponding incremental earnings if exercise is modeled.

audit_findings.title: The executive retirement obligation is an unfunded prior employee claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $17.0 million accrued obligation, equal to $0.30 per valuation share and 0.36% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: To the extent future benefit payments are not reflected in forecast OE, the unfunded accrued obligation should reduce surplus cash or the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Approximately $ 17.0 million and $ 16.9 million are accrued in Other liabilities for this plan on December 27, 2025 and December 28, 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is demonstrated and prior service expense may already be reflected in accounting earnings, but the full accrued amount is only 0.36% of base equity value. A complete bridge deduction would reduce value by about $0.30 per share and therefore would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the expected cash-payment schedule and whether forecast OE includes those payments; if not, deduct the $17.0 million obligation or its appropriately discounted unpaid amount from the bridge.
